title: Lead Time/Shipping/FAQ – Defiant Machine Works
text: LEADTIME Once the order is in our hands, it will be completed in 2 weeks or less. You will be contacted and updated if we encounter any issues or slowdowns while working on your firearm. Do you offer expedited or rushed services?Yes, we do. Pricing is listed below. Please email sales@defiantmachineworks.com to order rushed services, as we want to be sure we can meet your timeline.1 Week – $1253 Day – $22524HR Turnaround – $350 Do you offer in-person drop-off or pick-up if I am local?Yes, we do. When placing your order, you can use code “localdrop” so you don’t have to pay shipping. Once the order is placed, you will be contacted via text or email to schedule a time to drop off your firearm. SHIPPING Once you place an order, you will receive full shipping instructions via email, but here are a few notes. Shipping process for FIREARMS/SERIALIZED FRAMES:It is federally legal for you to ship directly to us. However, changes to UPS and FedEx policies make it more secure for all involved to use a local FFL (gun shop, pawn shop, gunsmith, etc.). We would greatly appreciate it if you chose this route. It gives both parties more peace of mind. Having it shipped through an FFL is also often less expensive. Shipping process for SLIDES AND NON-SERIALIZED PARTS: (SIG grip modules with FCU removed and 2011 grips removed from the frame)Feel free to ship USPS or UPS. Who is responsible for shipping costs?The shipping charge you see at checkout is for us to send the completed firearm, frame, or slide back to you. You will still be responsible for paying to ship the firearm, frame, or slide to us. Please see our shipping directions for how to ship those. FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS Once the order is in our hands, it will be completed in 2 weeks or less. You will be contacted and updated if we encounter any issues or slowdowns while working on your firearm. Can I edit an order once I place it? We highly recommend that you know what you want before placing an order. Depending on our workload, we might have already started work on your firearms, so we can’t guarantee that we will be able to make changes, though here is our general rule. Local drop-off orders have a 24-hour window to make changes to the order. Shipped orders have a 72-hour window to make changes to the order. Can I cancel my order? If you cancel your order before shipping your firearm to us, you will receive a refund of 75% of the order total. Once the firearm has been shipped to us, the order is non-refundable. Can you fix a bad stipple job or update my current stippling?You should email us photos at sales@defiantmachineworks.com so we can check them out and tell you what we think can be done. It all depends on the firearm’s model and what has already been done. Do you charge a Disassembly/Reassembly fee?We do not charge a disassembly/reassembly fee for all services listed on the site. Can you re-mill an existing optic cut or a factory optic cut?No, once a slide has been milled, we cannot mill it for something else.For Glock MOS slides, we can remove the locating studs to make them 507k footprint compatible. What is Cerakote?Cerakote is a ceramic-based finish that protects various surfaces. It is known for its excellent resistance to wear, corrosion, and chemicals, making it ideal for harsh environments. The application process involves spray coating, which allows for a wide range of colors and custom designs. Cerakote also enhances the item’s aesthetic appeal while maintaining its functionality. I want a camo or Cerakote job that is different from what is listed.Please email us at sales@defiantmachineworks.com or call/text us at 931-266-2422 to discuss your custom Cerakote needs. What color Cerakote do you offer?Cerakote offers many colors. Please click HERE to see all the options.

What rights you have over your data If you have an account on this site, or have left comments, you can request to receive an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us. You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you. This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal, or security purposes. text: Skip to content D95 Compensator for Glock Gen 5-6 $105.00 Precision-machined compensator for Gen 5 & 6 Glocks, 1/2×28 thread. Black finish. Reduces muzzle rise and keeps you on target. Ships ready to install. Description The Defiant Machine Works D95 is designed to fit the contour of the Glock Gen 6 AND Gen 5 slides. The D95 was made in collaboration with Herrington Arms using their proven and effective comp design but adding our aestetic touch. The D95 will work with the stock springs provided your gun has gone through our recommended break in period of 500 rounds of factory new ammunition with the threaded barrel you intend to use with the firearm before installing a compensator. We’ve found that this compensator has a 34% muzzle flip reduction depending on what 9mm load and Glock model is used. Specifications Material : 7075 Aluminum Finish : Black Anodized Compatibility : Models: Glock 17/19/26/45/34/19x/47 (including the MOS models of) with 1/2-28 Barrels and must be GEN 5 or GEN 6 Glocks Included : 5/64 Allen key – Steel replacement 8-32 set screw Length : 1.0″ long Holster Compatibility : Will fit in most open bottom holsters. We use Tier 1 Concealed, and Safariland. Will not work with aftermarket slides. Highlights Designed to work with most 1/2-28 threaded 9mm barrels. Made from USA-sourced 7075 aluminum. Designed, assembled, and machined in the USA. 3 port design to mitigate vertical and felt recoil NOT COMPATIBLE WITH SILENCERCO, BAR-STO, KKM, OR EFK BARRELS! Works with all gen 5 and Gen 6 Glock 9mm models AMMO DISCLAIMER: We DO NOT recommend using plated, bi-metal, or frangible ammo in ANY of our compensators. Doing so will void the warranty and we will not cover or replace the comp if there are any damages. INSTALLATION INSTRUCTIONS Make sure all threads are clean of grease, carbon, and loctite. Wipe the threads down till they’re clean. If the threads are not cleaned, the loctite will not set properly. Only use loctite 243 on the barrel AND set screw threads. Some versions of the blue Loctite are not very strong and will not hold up. Feel free to use a generous amount. Torque the set screws to no more than 18in/lbs. Allow the loctite to set for 24-48 hours before using. Please be sure that the compensator is not touching the slide, frame, or guide rod as that can cause cycling issues. When it comes to protecting and personalizing your firearms, tools, and outdoor gear, Cerakote has become the go-to choice for enthusiasts and professionals alike. But what exactly is Cerakote, and why should you consider it over other coating options? What is H Series Cerakote? Cerakote is a polymer-ceramic coating that provides superior durability, corrosion resistance, and a stunning finish. The H Series (what we use most) is specifically designed for firearms and is the most popular Cerakote product on the market. It offers excellent abrasion resistance, chemical resistance, and heat resistance, making it ideal for protecting your valuable gear in even the toughest conditions. Why Choose Cerakote Over Other Coating Options? Durability: Cerakote is known for its exceptional durability. While some coatings may chip or fade over time, Cerakote bonds to the surface of your item, ensuring it stays intact and looking great for years to come. Customization: One of the standout features of Cerakote is its versatility. With a vast array of colors and finishes, you can customize your items to reflect your personal style or brand. Whether you want a classic matte black finish or a vibrant, multi-colored design, Cerakote can deliver. Corrosion and Chemical Resistance: Cerakote is designed to withstand harsh environments and resist corrosion caused by moisture, salt, and chemicals. This makes it an excellent choice for firearms and outdoor gear that may be exposed to the elements. Heat Resistance: Cerakote can withstand high temperatures without degrading, making it an ideal choice for items such as suppressors and barrels that may experience significant heat during use. Easy Maintenance: Cerakote is easy to clean and maintain, ensuring your items look great with minimal effort. Get Creative with Cerakote One of the most exciting aspects of Cerakote is the creative possibilities it offers. You can mix and match colors, patterns, and finishes to create a truly unique look for your items. Whether you want a sleek, tactical design or a more artistic approach, the only limit is your imagination. Conclusion If you’re looking for a durable, customizable, and visually stunning coating for your firearms, tools, or outdoor gear, Cerakote is the answer. With its H Series product line, you can enjoy the best of both worlds: exceptional protection and endless creative possibilities. text: Skip to content Search $0.00 0 Cart September 22, 2025 The Art of Stippling: What is it and why does it matter? What is Stippling? Introduction As a serious shooter, you know that every detail of your firearm can impact your performance. One often-overlooked feature is stippling—the process of creating textured patterns on a firearm’s grip. In this blog post, we’ll explore what stippling is, its benefits for serious shooters, and the process of applying it. What is Stippling? Stippling refers to the process of creating a textured surface on the grip of a firearm, typically done on polymer frames. This technique enhances grip and control, providing a more secure hold during shooting. Stippling can take various forms, from simple dots to intricate patterns, and can be customized to fit the shooter’s preferences. Why You Want Stippling as a Serious Shooter Improved Grip and Control: Stippling enhances the texture of the grip, reducing the likelihood of slippage during firing. This is especially important in high-stress situations or adverse weather conditions. Customized Fit: Every shooter has unique preferences. Stippling allows for a personalized grip that can enhance comfort and control, ultimately improving overall shooting performance. Enhanced Aesthetics: Stippling can transform the look of your firearm, making it stand out and reflect your style. Increased Resale Value: A well-done stippling job can increase your firearm’s resale value, as it demonstrates attention to detail and customization. How Stippling is Done Stippling can be done by professionals or as a DIY project, but it requires careful attention to detail. Here’s a brief overview of the process: Preparation: We completely disassemble the firearm. Cutting the Borders: We cut the borders. (What you could consider the outline of the stippling). This gives a defined edge and keeps everything super clean. Stitching: Stitching is where we take a soldering iron with a special tip and run it around the border that we just cut in. This greatly aids in refining the final outline and provides a buffer area for where we will apply the stippling. Applying the Stippling: The heated tool is pressed onto the grip, and using a special tip, it creates the specific stipple pattern. This step requires precision and patience to ensure an even texture. Finishing Touches: Once the stippling is complete, we perform a quality check and address any high spots to ensure everything feels uniform. The grip is then cleaned and reassembled with the firearm. Conclusion Stippling is an art form that can significantly enhance your shooting experience. Whether you’re looking to improve grip and control, customize your firearm, or simply elevate its aesthetics, stippling is a worthwhile investment for serious shooters. text: Skip to content Search $0.00 0 Cart September 30, 2025 Understanding Optic Cuts for Pistols: What They Are, Why You Need One, and the Benefits of Direct Milling. What is an Optic Cut? An optic cut refers to a modification made to the slide of a pistol to allow for the mounting of an optical sight, such as a red dot sight. This cut typically involves machining a slot or pocket into the slide, which provides a secure and stable platform for the optic. Optic cuts can be made on various types of pistols, used for self-defense, competition, or duty. Why Would You Want an Optic Cut? Enhanced Accuracy: Optics can significantly improve your accuracy, especially at longer distances. They help you maintain focus on your target instead of your front sight. Faster Target Acquisition: With an optic, you can acquire your sights more quickly, enabling quicker shots on target. This is particularly useful in competitive shooting or self-defense scenarios. Increased Situational Awareness: With a red dot sight, you can keep both eyes open, which improves your peripheral vision and overall situational awareness. Customization: Optic cuts allow you to choose the optic that best suits your needs, whether it’s for competition, self-defense, or recreational shooting. Why Choose Direct Milling Over Factory Optic Plate Options? Improved Stability: Direct milling creates a more stable mounting platform than factory optic plates, which can sometimes flex or shift during use. This stability ensures that your optic remains zeroed, even after extensive shooting. Lower Profile: Direct milling enables a more streamlined profile, resulting in a reduced overall height of the optic. This can improve your draw speed and overall ergonomics when using the pistol. No Need for Adapters: Factory optic plates often require adapters to fit certain optics, which can add weight and increase the overall height of the setup. Direct milling eliminates the need for these adapters, resulting in a cleaner, more efficient setup. Customization Options: Direct milling enables more customization options, including the ability to select the precise location of the optic on the slide. This can enhance the overall user experience and make the pistol more comfortable to shoot. Aesthetics: A direct-milled optic cut can create a more professional and polished appearance compared to factory optic plates, which can sometimes look bulky or out of place. Conclusion Optic cuts for pistols are an excellent upgrade for shooters looking to enhance their accuracy, speed, and overall shooting experience. By choosing direct milling over factory optic plate options, you can benefit from improved stability, a lower profile, and greater customization options. No matter what you use your firearm for, an optic cut can take your pistol to the next level. PrevPreviousThe Art of Stippling: What is it and why does it matter? What is Stippling?
